records.text: Wiley the Black is a rogue in Lakeshire who acknowledges owing Gryan Stoutmantle a favor. Wiley supplies intelligence about the Defias Brotherhood, reporting that the gang has been working with gnolls, kobolds and goblins. Wiley warns that sharing this information could cost Wiley’s life and sends Stoutmantle a note explaining what is known.

Gath’Ilzogg is Warlord of the Blackrock Clan, boasting of the clan’s might and threatening intruders with death. Lakeshire’s wanted notice identifies Gath’Ilzogg as leader of the attacks on Stonewatch Keep and raids against the township. Targorr the Dread is described as a former supreme executioner serving under Gath’Ilzogg.
Singe is a dragonkin found in the Redridge Mountains.

Foreman Oslow is a Lakeshire foreman focused on rebuilding the Everstill Bridge during the orc siege. A shipment of his tools sank when the boat carrying them was struck, and he seeks help recovering his toolbox. He also needs iron pikes and rivets for the bridge effort, urging the workers to get it rebuilt.

Martie Jainrose is Lakeshire’s herbalist, with a garden she tends for its daffodils, her favorite flowers. She is furious that Bellygrub has trampled and pillaged it, and asks for the boar’s tusk as proof that the pest has been dealt with. Martie also provides a daffodil bouquet for Darcy, keeping its intended giver and recipient private as requested.

Chef Breanna is a Lakeshire cook known for Redridge Goulash. During the recent orc uprising, she fed the Stormwind brigade, leaving her cupboard bare. She asks for condor meat, goretusk snouts, and spider meat so she can prepare the dish, and calls the finished goulash a delicacy.

Magistrate Solomon is a Lakeshire magistrate confronting a township under constant siege. Uneasy that Stormwind’s army has not arrived, he seeks help from the Westfall militia and Darkshire’s Night Watch, and his correspondence leaves him suspecting that something is amiss in the kingdom.

Barkeep Daniels tends a Lakeshire tavern. With the orc invasion delaying his liquor shipment, he asks for supplies from several nearby settlements; he says his wife made a cloak as thanks for the errand.
Zem Leeward’s fishing remarks note that nothing is biting and invite the fish to “come to papa.”

Corporal Keeshan of the 12th Sabre Regiment is badly wounded and held captive after orcs overwhelmed the regiment. Keeshan seeks help returning to Redridge, explaining that grave injuries limit the pace. In the return speech, Keeshan reports for duty to Marshal Marris and thanks the rescuer, expecting Marris to reward the aid.

Darcy is a waitress who prepares lunch for Guard Parker but considers the roads too dangerous to deliver it herself. She is delighted by his bouquet, then recognizes daffodils as Martie’s favorite flowers and fears that the jealous Martie might have poisoned them if told whom they were for. She thanks the messenger and offers a meal.

Dockmaster Baren trades in Lake Everstill's spotted sunfish and is running low. He sees the growing murloc presence along the shore as a threat to the fishery, though he wonders whether the murlocs may be fleeing something themselves.

Marshal Marris directs Lakeshire’s response to Blackrock attacks in Redridge. He targets Tharil'zun, leader of the Blackrock Outrunners, and seeks to remove the shadowcasters’ demon-tainted Midnight Orbs from the conflict and have them destroyed. He thanks those who help Corporal Keeshan escape the orcs, regarding that rescue as service to the Kingdom.

Morganth is a powerful mage living in Redridge’s Tower of Ilgalar. Lakeshire’s authorities accuse him of using arcane magic to terrorize the town and controlling the Shadowhide gnolls. Theocritus identifies Shadowhide pendants as a means of communication between the gnolls and their master, Morganth. Another account describes a rival seeking to spy on Morganth and learn his plans.

Verner Osgood keeps horses at a stable near Lakeshire and fears the Redridge gnolls that take them when they stray. He wants their leader Yowler killed to scatter the pack. He resents Argus’s demand for payment for shoes sent from Goldshire, but seeks black dragon whelp scales to settle the debt, worried that Argus will send someone to collect it.
A flesh-eating murloc of Redridge.
A Redridge Mongrel is a gnoll found along the southern roads of Redridge, where Deputy Feldon considers the gnoll camps a threat to assess. It growls about fresh meat and more bones to gnaw on.
A Redridge Poacher is a gnoll camping along Redridge’s southern roads. Deputy Feldon wants the gnoll threat assessed and reduced. The poacher growls about fresh meat and more bones to gnaw on.

A Redridge gnoll brute, this one meets an intruder with hungry threats about fresh meat and bones. Its brief snarls and predatory taunts suit a creature that answers a challenge with menace rather than conversation.
A Shadowhide darkweaver who greets intruders with hungry, snarling threats about fresh meat and bones.
A Redridge gnoll mystic who snarls hungry threats about fresh meat and bones.
A Shadowhide slayer who answers intruders with snarls and threats of fresh meat and bones, and finishes off a badly wounded foe with a killing blow.
A Shadowhide brute whose taunts promise fresh meat and bones. Its few words are snarls, blunt and predatory.
A Shadowhide Gnoll snarls and calls out for fresh meat and more bones to gnaw.
A Rabid Shadowhide Gnoll that snarls about fresh meat and bones to gnaw, and poisons its foes.
A Blackrock Champion, a leader of a Blackrock unit, who boasts of the Blackrock Orcs' power and taunts challengers as no match for them. It fights under a Devotion Aura.
A Blackrock Shadowcaster who boasts of the Blackrock Orcs' power and warns challengers they are no match. This spellcaster hurls Shadow Bolts.
A Blackrock Renegade who boasts of the Blackrock Orcs' power and warns challengers they are no match. It can fly into a frenzy in battle.
A Blackrock Orc combatant who boasts that opponents cannot match the Blackrock Orcs and calls on their power. Its combat behavior can include a frenzy.
A young black dragon that spits Fireballs.
A Redridge Alpha whose snarls threaten fresh meat and bones to gnaw. It strikes hard in a fight.
A Redridge basher whose combat barks threaten fresh meat and bones to gnaw. It can rend opponents in combat.

Guard Parker is a Stormwind guard charged with patrolling the road from Lakeshire toward Duskwood. He has seen gnoll encampments north and east of the road and urges Lakeshire to learn of the gathering force. Darcy sends him lunch while he is on patrol; Parker warmly credits her kindness and says the work of guarding Lakeshire from orcs and gnolls is tough.
A Blackrock outrunner of Redridge who taunts opponents with the power of the Blackrock Orcs and boasts that they are no match for them.

Tharil’zun is the orc leader of the Blackrock Outrunners. Marshal Marris reports ambushes by the Outrunners and Renegades on the approaches to Stonewatch Keep, and seeks Tharil’zun’s head to remove their leader.
Verner Osgood identifies Yowler as the leader of a gnoll pack hunting in the hills above Lakeshire. He singles out Yowler’s louder cry and warns that this leader is no ordinary mongrel.
A murloc nightcrawler in the Redridge Mountains.
A murloc tidecaller in the Redridge Mountains.
A minor murloc tidecaller in the Redridge Mountains.
A Shadowhide warrior in the Redridge Mountains who snarls at opponents as “fresh meat” and anticipates more bones to gnaw on.
A murloc scout in the Redridge Mountains.
A Shadowhide assassin in the Redridge Mountains who snarls at opponents as “fresh meat” and anticipates more bones to gnaw on.
A Redridge drudger who snarls at opponents as “fresh meat” and anticipates more bones to gnaw on.
Kazon is a rare humanoid who backhands his foes.
A Blackrock tracker in the Redridge Mountains who boasts of the Blackrock Orcs’ power and taunts opponents as no match for them.
Chatter is a rare beast that poisons and paralyzes its prey.

Lieutenant Fangore is named in Magistrate Solomon’s wanted notice as leader of the Shadowhide Gnoll Clan, working under Morganth. The notice accuses Fangore of betraying Stormwind and calls for his death.
Ardo Dirtpaw in the Redridge Mountains snarls at opponents as “fresh meat” and anticipates more bones to gnaw on.
The Redridge Thrasher's cries mix rough growls with threats about fresh meat and bones.

Amy Davenport is a tradeswoman who welcomes Antonio as a familiar visitor, glad he has made it safely back. Her farewell suggests she expects to see him again in about a week; she also offers goods to browse.
Kimberly Hiett is a fletcher who offers goods, ammunition, and repairs. Her work centers on bows and related supplies, with repair service alongside her trade.
Karen Taylor supplies blacksmithing and mining goods. Her shop serves craftspeople and miners looking for the materials and tools associated with those trades.
Lindsay Ashlock deals in general supplies, including ammunition. Her broad stock makes her a source for everyday goods as well as ranged weapon needs.
Kara Adams is a shield crafter who sells goods and offers repairs. Her trade is centered on shields, giving her shop a more specialized focus than a general outfitter.
Alma Jainrose is a herbalism trainer who offers to instruct interested visitors in the craft.
A demon known as a Servant of Ilgalar in Redridge.
Nathan is a humanoid in Redridge Mountains.
Madison is a humanoid in Redridge Mountains.
Rachel is a humanoid in Redridge Mountains.
Erin is a humanoid in Redridge Mountains.
Hannah is a humanoid in Redridge Mountains.

Guard Berton distrusts the political hold delaying Targorr the Dread’s execution. He regards the former executioner’s survival as a threat of foul play and argues that justice may require action beyond a courtroom clouded by noble influence.

Bailiff Conacher presents Lakeshire’s legal case against Morganth and the Shadowhide gnolls: aiding a criminal of the Kingdom is punishable under local law. His appeal treats enforcement as a civic duty and the Court of Lakeshire as the authority behind that justice.

Guard Howe is involved in Lakeshire’s campaign against the Blackrock Clan, rewarding help against its Champions. He says Marshal Marris expects Stormwind’s reserve to arrive soon, reflecting the township’s reliance on reinforcements as the conflict continues.
Ariena Stormfeather is a gryphon master in Redridge who offers flight travel. In danger, Ariena calls for guards and summons enraged gryphons.

Guard Ashlock reports heavy Blackrock activity in the east and voices concern about the delayed Stormwind reinforcements. The brief report places this guard among those watching the local threat and awaiting support.
Guard Hiett hopes that reinforcements from Stormwind will arrive soon.
Guard Clarke is a guard in Lakeshire.
Guard Pearce reports no sign of Stormwind's 2nd Battalion and reports Shadowhide movement in the northeast.
Guard Adams is a guard in Lakeshire.
Rohh the Silent is a rare, stealthy humanoid who fights with poison.
Dorin Songblade is an armorer in the Redridge Mountains who sells goods and repairs equipment.

Deputy Feldon patrols Lakeshire’s approaches and handles reports for the Stormwind Army. A report of gnoll encampments prompts him to send a scout into southern Redridge to count the force and assess its threat. He regards the gnolls as a danger that could reach Elwynn and knows Lakeshire is ill equipped to respond.
A murloc shorestriker is a hostile shoreline creature that charges at foes and flees for help when badly wounded.
Lamar Veisilli is Lakeshire's fruit seller, selling fruit to passersby.
Vernon Hale supplies fishing gear.
Matthew Hooper trains fishers. When an experienced angler has outgrown his instruction, he points them toward Old Man Heming’s book in Booty Bay or Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh for further guidance.
Clyde Ranthal sells leatherworking supplies in Redridge to local leatherworkers.
Gloria Femmel sells cooking supplies to anyone who wants to cook.
Gretchen Vogel is a waitress who also sells food. Her work connects serving visitors with supplying the meals and provisions they need.

Crystal Boughman is a cooking trainer who speaks warmly of cooking as a lifelong pursuit. She offers instruction and points aspiring cooks toward Shandrina in Silverwind Refuge for the Expert Cookbook, and Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan as a master of the culinary arts.
Henry Chapal is a gunsmith whose services include ammunition and repairs. His work supports visitors maintaining and equipping their firearms.
Sherman Femmel is a butcher who also sells food. His trade supplies visitors with provisions, alongside the practical work of preparing meat.
Gerald Crawley sells poison supplies. His specialized stock distinguishes his trade from ordinary provisions vendors.
Franklin Hamar is a tailoring-supplies merchant. His goods are available to browse, giving customers a direct source for tailoring materials.
The Captured Servant of Azora is a captive who sells specialist tailoring supplies.
Bernard Brubaker is a leather armor merchant. He offers goods to browse and can repair equipment, making him a practical source for both armor and its upkeep.
A Blackrock orc scout who boasts of the Blackrock Orcs' strength and tells challengers they are no match. It shoots from range, can work itself into a frenzy, and flees for help when badly hurt.
A Blackrock orc sentry who boasts of its people's power and tells challengers they cannot win. It can fly into a frenzy when fighting.
A Blackrock Orc Hunter, it boasts of the Orcs' power and warns opponents they are no match. It attacks by throwing weapons, bringing a hunter's role into its fighting.
A Blackrock Orc combatant who invokes the power of the Blackrock Orcs and can summon an imp. In battle, this summoner presents its side as a force to be reckoned with.
A Blackrock orc gladiator who boasts of the Blackrock Orcs' power and tells opponents they are no match. A frontline fighter that bellows Battle Shouts.
Roger is a humanoid in the Redridge Mountains.
Jamin is a humanoid in the Redridge Mountains.
Bartender Wental serves food and drink at the inn.

Yorus Barleybrew runs the Rethban Gauntlet, a timed trial into the caverns that requires challengers to reach the first fork and return alive. He insists they first drink his family's Barleybrew Scalder, then celebrates successful runs publicly. He promises a reward through his friend Furen Longbeard, a shieldsmith in Stormwind.
Wilma Ranthal is a Lakeshire skinning trainer.
Innkeeper Brianna welcomes weary travelers to the Lakeshire inn, offering rooms and goods, and joins in the seasonal Trick or Treat.
Narnie is a beast associated with Lakeshire.

Lucius is an SI:7 associate in Lakeshire who trains thieves and prepares new rogues for field work. He supplies thieving tools and sends a trainee to Alther’s Mill to recover a token from his lockbox, then judges the trainee’s skill with dry, cutting humor. He warns that Blackrock orcs may be near the mill, while making clear that inexperience, rather than danger, is no excuse for failure.

Arantir, known as the Hand of Chaos, seeks the Horns of Nez’ra, an artifact stolen from Ravenholdt Manor. He says he searched across continents and oceans before learning Blackrock orcs had the horns, and urges their recovery. The relic’s return matters deeply to him: he describes denying it to Ravenholdt as unthinkable and presents success as a possible path toward the assassins’ company.

Hilary is a young girl in Lakeshire who misses a necklace her father gave her and worries that he will be angry she lost it. She fears the monsters her father says live in the lake, and asks whether they were beaten. When the necklace is found, she thanks the helper and says her kitty Effsee is grateful too.

Shawn is a child in Lakeshire who asks for help on behalf of his group of friends. The request is to find Hilary’s lost necklace; the accompanying account says they had been fishing together and had already searched nearby, while the children are forbidden to swim because of dangers their parents describe in the lake.
Penny is a stable master who offers help stabling pets and recovering lost companions.
Lakeshire Guard is one of the guards associated with Lakeshire.
Seeker Aqualon is an elemental of the Redridge Mountains.
Squiddic is a rare named humanoid found along the waters of the Redridge region. Badly hurt, it flees to find help.
Ribchaser is a rare named humanoid found along the waters of the Redridge region. Badly hurt, it flees to find help.
Snarlflare is a named creature found in the surrounding region. In combat, Snarlflare casts a spell.
Boulderheart is a named creature found in the surrounding region. In combat, Boulderheart casts a spell.

The Redridge Flame Warden tends the Alliance Midsummer flame and welcomes visitors who come to honor it. Its festival greeting urges Alliance visitors to honor fires across Alliance lands and to desecrate Horde flames, showing clear Alliance allegiance.

place_records.text: You are in Redridge Mountains, in the Eastern Kingdoms, where the Alliance holds some ground. Lakeshire is its only settlement here and it belongs to the Alliance. Blackrock orcs have attacked across the mountains, and gnolls, murlocs, black dragon whelps and dire condors are also dangerous.

You are in Lake Everstill, a lake in the Redridge Mountains famous for its spotted sunfish. Larger murloc groups are fishing its shores and threatening the lake's fish. Matthew Hooper trains fishers here.

You are in Lakeshire, a township under constant siege by Blackrock orcs. Its inn, stable and vendors serve the township, and Marshal Marris directs the response to the Blackrock attacks. Magistrate Solomon is still waiting for the Stormwind army to arrive.
You are in Stonewatch, in the Redridge Mountains, where Blackrock sentries and shadowcasters are common. A spirit healer here offers a return to life for a price.
You are in Stonewatch Falls, in the Redridge Mountains, where Shadowhide slayers and darkweavers share the ground with Blackrock renegades, outrunners and murlocs.

You are in Redridge Canyons, in the Redridge Mountains, where Corporal Keeshan of the 12th Sabre Regiment is held captive and badly wounded after orcs overwhelmed his regiment. Redridge bashers, mystics and brutes roam here alongside Blackrock champions.

You are in the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains, where servants of Ilgalar and Shadowhide gnolls wait. Morganth, who is said to be searching for the Scythe of Elune, is among those who make the tower dangerous.
You are in Alther's Mill, in the Redridge Mountains, where greater tarantulas, dire condors, black dragon whelps and Blackrock grunts roam.
You are in Render's Camp, in the Redridge Mountains, where Blackrock trackers, summoners and champions gather.
You are in Render's Valley, in the Redridge Mountains, where a captured servant of Azora offers tailoring supplies while Blackrock outrunners and grunts roam nearby.
You are in Render's Rock, in the Redridge Mountains, where Blackrock champions, trackers and summoners are found, along with the Kazon.
You are in Stonewatch Tower, in the Redridge Mountains, where Blackrock sentries and scouts watch the land alongside grunts and outrunners.

You are in Galardell Valley, in the Redridge Mountains, where Shadowhide warriors, gnolls and darkweavers are numerous. Rohh the Silent is among the threats, and Shadowhide brutes and rabid gnolls roam too.
You are in Lakeridge Highway, a stretch of road in Redridge Mountains. Redridge poachers, mongrels and thrashers prowl the road, and Black Dragon Whelps, ribchasers and dire condors range over it.

You are in Three Corners in Redridge Mountains, where a Stormwind guard named Guard Parker patrols the road from Lakeshire toward Duskwood. Tarantulas, Redridge thrashers, mongrels and ribchasers haunt the area, and gnoll encampments are gathering to the north and east of the road.
You are in Rethban Caverns, a cave system in the Redridge Mountains. Redridge drudgers, bashers and mystics prowl its depths, and Ardo Dirtpaw is a notable enemy among them.
You are in Stonewatch Keep, a fortified keep in the Redridge Mountains. Blackrock shadowcasters, sentries and hunters are a danger here, and Gath'Ilzogg is a notable Blackrock enemy among them.
